headline: Southborough adopted its FY27 tax rate while confronting an estimated $1.4 million FY28 budget gap and escalating school renovation projections.
synopsis: In November, Southborough set its FY27 property tax rate at a uniform $14.54 per thousand, while town and school officials warned that the upcoming FY28 budget faces a $1.4 million deficit that could force severe staffing and service cuts without an operational tax override. Architects presented updated estimates for the Neary Elementary School project, projecting renovation costs between $33 million and $40 million, far higher than earlier $15 million estimates. The Select Board advanced a proposed zoning bylaw amendment to Town Meeting to lift the town's cap on 55-plus senior housing developments. Meanwhile, planning officials reviewed updated traffic mitigation proposals for the 167,000-square-foot Costco project along Route 9. The town also celebrated a major grant win, securing up to $632,000 in state funding for proposed Fayville Memorial Park recreation improvements.

top_items.title: FY28 budget deficit and potential override
top_items.why: Town departments face a $1.4 million budget deficit for FY28, prompting officials to draft dual budgets that highlight steep service cuts if voters reject a tax override.
top_items.body: The Select Board and department heads reviewed preliminary FY28 operating requests under two distinct scenarios. Level-service Budget A projects a $1.4 million deficit requiring a Proposition 2 1/2 override, while level-funded Budget B would trigger severe cuts across departments. Fire officials warned Budget B would reduce shift staffing and sideline Southborough's second ambulance, the Police Department would lose an officer and dispatcher, and K-8 schools would face eliminating roughly 15 staff positions. Town officials are evaluating whether to pursue a multi-year override and are examining municipal reserve and revolving funds to soften the shortfall.

top_items.title: Neary School renovation cost estimates surge
top_items.why: Architects revealed that modernizing Neary Elementary School will cost between $33 million and $40 million, rendering earlier $15 million estimates unfeasible.
top_items.body: Tappe Architects presented detailed cost evaluations to the Elementary School Building Committee and School Committee, showing that bringing Neary's basic mechanical systems up to modern code would cost roughly $32.9 million. Their preferred Option 3 addition and renovation design, which infills the courtyard for a full-sized gymnasium and modernizes classrooms, is estimated at $39.8 million. Officials and school leaders are debating whether to pursue town-only financing or submit a Statement of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority in January 2027, balancing potential state aid against years of construction inflation.

top_items.title: FY27 single tax rate set at $14.54
top_items.why: The Select Board adopted a single tax rate of $14.54 per thousand, increasing the average single-family tax bill by an estimated 5.01 percent.
top_items.body: Following presentations from the Board of Assessors showing town valuation reaching $4.072 billion and the average single-family home value rising 3.7 percent to $1,027,800, the Select Board voted 4-1 to maintain a unified single tax rate rather than shifting taxes onto commercial properties. The board also voted 5-0 against adopting residential or small commercial exemptions. The decision translates to a projected average single-family residential tax bill increase of about 5.01 percent.

top_items.title: Senior housing zoning amendment advances
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously to sponsor a zoning bylaw amendment lifting Southborough's 7 percent cap on 55-plus housing developments.
top_items.body: The Select Board referred a zoning amendment drafted by the Affordable Housing Trust to the Planning Board and voted unanimously to sponsor it on the Town Meeting warrant. The proposal removes the current 7 percent municipal cap on age-restricted 55-plus housing, allows up to eight units per acre on parcels of at least two acres, and requires 10 percent open space alongside a mandatory 12.5 percent affordable housing component. The measure now heads to public hearings before the Planning Board.

top_items.title: Costco warehouse traffic modeling review
top_items.why: Costco presented revised regional traffic modeling for its proposed Route 9 warehouse, facing board and resident concerns over intersection failures and neighborhood cut-throughs.
top_items.body: The Planning Board reviewed an updated traffic impact study for Costco Wholesale's proposed 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-position gas station at 21 Coslin Drive. Board members and abutters raised substantial concerns regarding traffic delays, failing levels of service at nearby Route 9 intersections, and heavy truck and customer cut-through traffic along local residential streets. Proposed developer mitigations include paving and restriping Crystal Pond Road and Coslin Drive, adjusting Route 9 traffic signal timing, and funding a post-opening traffic evaluation. The public hearing was continued to November 16.

top_items.title: State awards $632,000 grant for Fayville Park
top_items.why: Southborough received a state grant covering half of the projected costs for splash pad, dog park, and walking trail upgrades at Fayville Memorial Park.
top_items.body: The town was awarded a Land and Water Conservation Fund grant of up to $632,000 to redevelop Fayville Memorial Park. The project plan features Southborough's first municipal splash pad, an enclosed dog park, walking paths, and accessible infrastructure. The Recreation Commission plans to seek matching Community Preservation Act funds at the 2027 Annual Town Meeting and is coordinating with the Select Board, police, and DPW on parking solutions along Central Street to protect park open space.

top_items.title: Seniors oppose municipal department consolidation
top_items.why: Residents voiced strong opposition to merging the Senior Center or Council on Aging with other municipal departments during a governance study listening session.
top_items.body: During a public listening session led by the town's governance study consultant, dozens of senior center participants objected to any recommendations that would consolidate the Council on Aging with Recreation or Youth and Family Services. Residents argued that seniors account for roughly 20 percent of Southborough's population and have specialized service needs that require departmental autonomy. Attendees also raised concerns over municipal communication, town website navigation, and budget oversight as the consultant prepares final recommendations for December 15.
